subject: System Design
title: Foreign Keys and Referential Integrity
description: A quick win: understand Foreign Keys and Referential Integrity.

hook.text: An order references user ID 42, but user 42 doesn't exist. The order points to a ghost.

buildup.text: A foreign key constraint ensures that references between tables always point to valid rows.

discovery.text: If you try to delete user 42 while orders reference them, the database blocks the delete.

twist.text: NoSQL databases don't enforce foreign keys. Application code must handle referential integrity manually.

climax.text: Foreign keys are the database's way of saying: no orphans allowed. Every reference must be valid.

punchline.text: Foreign keys prevent references to data that doesn't exist.

quiz.question: What does a foreign key constraint prevent?
options: References to rows that don't exist
